newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia to speed sell-off of sprawling coal mine.
newsitem.headline: Colombia to speed sell-off of sprawling coal mine.

text.p: A government source said Tuesday that Colombia would speed up the previously announced privatization of its sprawling Cerrejon Zona coal mine as part of an ongoing bid to get its financial house in order.
The mine, which produces about 15 million tonnes of coal a year, is the largest open pit coal mine in Latin America.
It had originally been targeted for privatization in late 1997 but the source, a spokesman for President Ernesto Samper, said the deal would now take place much earlier.
A virtual mountain of bureaucratic paperwork that promised to delay the sale for months was overriden by a decree Samper issued late Tuesday, the source told Reuters.
He did not elaborate and the text of the decree, issued under terms of the state of economic emergency Samper declared last month, was not immediately available.

But a source close to the government's privatization committee said an investment bank would be selected by the government in mid-March to ensure that the Cerrejon sell-off gets under way as quickly as possible.
The state of economic emergency, which Samper announced on January 13, was called to help the government adopt urgent and extraordinary measures aimed at cutting its burgeoning fiscal deficit.
